discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (moiré materials, flat-band superconductivity)
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, two graphene layers develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions overwhelm kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this dramatically, observing correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This theory-first, experiment-confirmed discovery created the field of twistronics and moiré quantum matter, now reproduced across many laboratories and material platforms: twisted multilayer graphene, transition-metal dichalcogenide moirés hosting fractional Chern insulators, and more. It has given physicists a tunable laboratory for strongly correlated and topological phases, and revealed that superconductivity in flat bands is governed by the quantum geometry of Bloch states rather than band dispersion alone. Few recent discoveries have so profoundly opened new research directions, uniting band topology, electron correlations and superconductivity in a single, controllable system.
